hook: *Rs 36 crore* of diesel saved by tracking how RTC drivers drive
hook_b: *Rs 36 crore* of diesel saved by tracking how RTC drivers drive
tldr: TGSRTC says i-ALERT, fitted in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses, grades every driver after duty and has saved about Rs 36 crore of diesel.

beats.what: The system tracks gear choice, staying in the Green Band RPM range, idling, overspeeding and harsh braking; drivers get a grade and feedback after each duty.
beats.why: Fuel is one of the biggest running costs for a bus fleet, and TGSRTC says it is the first state RTC in India to use the system.
beats.care: If you ride TGSRTC buses, the same tracking that cuts fuel also flags overspeeding and harsh braking on your trip.

causes.label: Diesel is a top running cost for RTC

effects.label: ~1.98 lakh litres diesel saved a month

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TGSRTC puts the monthly saving at nearly 1,98,090 litres of diesel, about Rs 2 crore a month.

cards.q: Should every driver's driving be graded by software after each shift?

qs: Do graded drivers get any reward, or only feedback?
Will the 1,500-bus figure grow to the rest of the fleet?

facts.t: i-ALERT buses save nearly *1,98,090 litres* of diesel a month, TGSRTC says.
Annual CO2 cut is projected at *6,169.84 tonnes*.

viz.verdict: Only Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses have the system so far
Less emission from the same fleet, good for city air

learn.t: Green Band RPM = the engine-speed range where a bus burns the least fuel

watch: TGSRTC's MD asked other wings to adopt similar tech; AP and Karnataka RTCs are studying the results.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: TGSRTC saves Rs 36 crore in diesel costs using i-ALERT technology in 1,500 buses

fact: TGSRTC says driver-tracking tech in *1,500* buses saved *Rs 36 crore* in diesel
twist: Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka's RTCs have already asked TGSRTC how the system performs.
